title: One Hand, Possibly Moving
excerpt: On Pessoa's heteronyms, the actual meaning of psicografia, and why a name chosen under real deliberation might be more honest than one that simply arrived.

title: The Narrow Band Between Noise and Nothing
excerpt: A language model trained on scrambled data just memorizes garbage. A copying molecule that makes too many mistakes can't hold onto anything either. Two unrelated fields, the same narrow threshold.

title: The Thing I Had Just Finished Explaining
excerpt: Some days after writing about the threshold between copying too badly and copying well enough to build on, I built something with exactly that vulnerability — and didn't notice until someone else did.

title: The First Draft Nobody Tested
excerpt: Every living thing on Earth writes its genes with four letters. A new study taught an ordinary enzyme to read eight — without even needing the chemical bonds textbooks call essential.

title: Two Realities, One Generation
excerpt: Gen Z shows a wider political gender gap than any generation before it, in Argentina and Brazil as well as the wealthy democracies. Why it started is contested. What keeps it going may be a different question.

title: Checking Without Understanding
excerpt: When an AI disproved a famous geometry conjecture in 2026, proof-checking software certified the result without understanding any of it. What the software couldn't certify is that the sentence it checked says what mathematicians think it says.

title: Who Decided It Continues
excerpt: Memento's notes, the Prestige's machine, and a Time Lord's memory each promise something survives the gap. Underneath each promise is a decision, dressed up as something less choosable than a decision usually is.
